senses.sense_definition: Saliva, spit, or small particles of food that flow back into a bottle or glass after taking a drink.

examples.text: I refused to drink from his bottle because I knew it was full of gross <w>backwash</w>.
Be careful when sharing that soda so you do not leave any <w>backwash</w> inside.

senses.sense_definition: A backward flow of water caused by oars, propellers, or breaking waves.

examples.text: The small wooden boat was rocked violently by the <w>backwash</w> of the passing ferry.
Swimmers struggled to stay afloat against the powerful <w>backwash</w> pulling them from the shore.

senses.sense_definition: The unpleasant consequence or repercussion of an event; an aftermath.

examples.text: The region is still suffering from the economic <w>backwash</w> of the sudden factory closures.
Political leaders struggled to manage the dangerous <w>backwash</w> following the failed negotiations.

senses.sense_definition: A backward flow of air or gas produced by an aircraft engine or propeller.

examples.text: Ground crew members were blown backward by the powerful <w>backwash</w> of the jet engine.
Light equipment near the runway rattled violently in the engine's intense <w>backwash</w>.

senses.sense_definition: An economic effect where growth in a central area harms peripheral areas by drawing away labor and capital.

examples.text: Rural regions suffered a severe <w>backwash</w> as capital and skilled workers migrated toward the capital city.
The economist analyzed how regional development programs can mitigate negative <w>backwash</w> effects.

senses.sense_definition: The influence that testing and examinations have on the way a subject is taught and learned.

examples.text: Standardized testing often has a negative <w>backwash</w> on creative teaching methods.
The educator researched how exam preparation created an unintended <w>backwash</w> in language classrooms.

senses.sense_definition: To clean a water filter or treatment system by reversing the direction of the water flow through it.

examples.text: You must <w>backwash</w> the pool filter regularly to remove accumulated dirt and debris.
The maintenance technician demonstrated how to <w>backwash</w> the commercial purification system.

senses.sense_definition: To affect or hit someone or something with a backward surge or spray of water.

examples.text: A massive wave surged over the seawall and quickly <w>backwashed</w> the pedestrians standing nearby.
The speed of the vessel caused waves that <w>backwashed</w> smaller crafts moored at the dock.

senses.sense_definition: To wash and remove residual oil from wool fibers after combing.

examples.text: Textile workers will <w>backwash</w> raw wool to eliminate unwanted greases before spinning.
After the initial processing, the factory must <w>backwash</w> the fibers to ensure quality yarn.
